bottleneck: Sickle cell CRISPR therapies work ex vivo — editing patients' stem cells outside the body — which requires toxic myeloablative conditioning and million-dollar manufacturing per patient. True in vivo editing of hematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow would democratize the cure, but no delivery system efficiently reaches long-term repopulating stem cells without editing the wrong lineages.
current_state: Ex vivo products are approved and curative for some, but access is minimal. In vivo HSC editing is preclinical, with delivery the hard problem.

sources.title: Gene therapies should be for all

title: Sickle cell cure trapped in ex vivo manufacturing
why_it_blocks: A cure that costs millions and requires a transplant center is not a cure for the millions with sickle cell, mostly in Africa. In vivo editing is the only path to scale.
